name: GHRP-6
summary: An early lab-made peptide that releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor, sold as a research chemical to raise growth hormone; human studies are small and short.
what_it_is: GHRP-6 is a synthetic peptide of six amino acids, including two mirror-image (D-form) amino acids. It came out of 1977 work on enkephalin-like (opioid-like) peptides and was the first growth hormone-releasing peptide with significant activity in the body. It acts on the ghrelin receptor to prompt the pituitary gland to release growth hormone, and it can briefly raise cortisol. It is not FDA-approved.

evidence.why: Small, short human studies show growth hormone release (weaker in obesity), brief cortisol rises and sleep changes; there are no trials of health outcomes.

status_us.label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
status_us.note: FDA lists GHRP-6 in Category 2 (significant safety risks) for outsourcing facilities and places it in Category 3 (nominated without adequate support) for ordinary compounding pharmacies, which leaves compounding open to FDA enforcement. WADA bans it in sport.

benefits.claim: Raised growth hormone release in adults with obesity, though less than in lean adults, alone or combined with GHRH
More stage 2 sleep with higher growth hormone in a small study of 7 healthy young men; other forms tested showed no sleep effect
Higher IGF-1 in 14 men on testosterone therapy who took it with GHRP-2 and sermorelin

risks.risk: FDA cites possible immune reactions from aggregation and impurities, plus concerns about cortisol and higher blood sugar from reduced insulin sensitivity
Brief rises in cortisol and ACTH (stress hormones)
Increased appetite and fat gain, which a review calls built into how ghrelin-type drugs work
No long-term, cancer or mortality safety data exist for growth hormone secretagogues
Black-market supply: a review reports ghrelin mimetics are sold on the black market, so identity and purity are uncertain

avoid_if: Diabetes or prediabetes (clinician first: may reduce insulin sensitivity)
Competitive athletes (prohibited by WADA at all times)

before: General health check with a clinician
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for GHRP-6; a review of growth hormone secretagogues advises tracking IGF-1 and blood sugar, and FDA flags effects on blood sugar and cortisol.

studies.title: The Safety and Efficacy of Growth Hormone Secretagogues
studies.people: Review of small human studies, including 19 adults with obesity and 7 healthy young men
studies.finding: Describes GHRP-6 as the first growth hormone-releasing peptide with significant activity in the body. Small studies showed a blunted growth hormone response in obesity and diabetes, brief cortisol rises and more stage 2 sleep.

studies.title: Growth Hormone Secretagogue Treatment in Hypogonadal Men Raises Serum Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1 Levels
studies.people: 14 men on testosterone therapy (retrospective chart review)
studies.finding: A combination of GHRP-6, GHRP-2 and sermorelin raised average IGF-1 from about 160 to 239 ng/mL; body composition was not assessed.

studies.title: Growth Hormone Doping in Sports: A Critical Review of Use and Detection Strategies
studies.finding: Describes GHRP-6 as a non-natural, enkephalin-derived hexapeptide; ghrelin mimetics have moderate effects on growth hormone and IGF-1, raise cortisol and appetite, and are sold on the black market.

ask_your_clinician: Would the appetite and cortisol effects work against my goals?
How would we watch my blood sugar and IGF-1?
Is there an approved treatment for my actual goal or diagnosis?

notes_for_editor: Primary studies (Bowers 1984 Endocrinology; Cordido studies in obesity; the sleep study) were not opened because PubMed links were blocked and the web-search budget ran out; findings come from the Sigalos review (source 6) and Baumann 2012. The prototype's 'strong hunger increase' and 'water retention' were not confirmed for GHRP-6 specifically: the review reports no GHRP-6-specific appetite or prolactin findings, and appetite is cited here only as a class effect. US status is split: 503B Category 2 but 503A Category 3; no 2025-2026 change was found. The D-amino-acid structure is from source 9.
